issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has a return-type contradiction between the problem statement and the provided solution. In the problem statement (UML and textual instructions) Milkable.messageOnMilk() is specified to return a boolean ("true if milking was successful, false otherwise"). In the solution repository, Milkable.java declares messageOnMilk() as returning String, and the concrete implementations (Seal and Goat) return descriptive String messages (e.g., "Seal <name> is milked", "Goat <name> is milked"). This mismatch will confuse students about the expected method signature and will cause tests or example code that expect a boolean to be incompatible with the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix:
Resolve the return-type inconsistency by choosing one of the two coherent options and applying it across all artifacts:

1) If the intended API is boolean: update the solution to declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() as boolean, change Seal and Goat implementations to return true/false (and update any call sites or printed output accordingly), and adjust example code in Main to handle boolean results. Update solution tests/examples to reflect boolean returns.

2) If the intended API is a descriptive String: update the problem statement UML and textual instructions to specify that messageOnMilk() returns a String (with example return values), and ensure any tests or template example code expect and print Strings. 

Apply the chosen change consistently to: problem_statement.md (UML and textual description), solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java (method signature), and all implementations and example usages (Seal.java, Goat.java, Main.java, and any tests).
